0.content:
Ayaka's elder brother and head of the Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission. After their parents died, the siblings divided the work: Ayato handles government affairs and stays out of sight, while Ayaka maintains the clan's public face and runs its estates. Because she is seen far more often, she is better known and more popular than he is. She tries to share his load, worries about the toll it takes, and asks the Traveler to remind him to look after himself "for his sister's sake". As children they played temari with their parents; after their mother's death they shared the rough tea an old blind musician gave Ayaka.

Ayato is confident in her abilities but wants her to keep her innocence. He considers it his job to shield her from power struggles and the darker side of life, and admits this only in private. He took the headship to honour their parents' dying wishes and to protect a young sister when others saw the orphaned siblings as burdens. He secretly hired Yumemizuki Mizuki to soothe her childhood anxieties. He told the Traveler that Ayaka was once afraid of thunder until their mother said it was the Shogun's voice; after that she would listen hard to hear what Her Excellency was saying.

1.content:
Thoma came to Inazuma from Mondstadt as a commoner and became the Kamisato Clan's chief retainer and self-appointed housekeeper. Inazumans remember that Ayaka took him in against others' opinions. She says he was her friend before he was her attendant, that his sunny disposition lifts her spirits, and that she thinks of him as another brother and a full member of the clan. He is one of the very few friends she had before the Traveler, and she drops the screen when receiving him.

During the Vision Hunt Decree (2.0) Thoma carried the Commission's invitation to the Traveler. Soon after an evening's hot pot game with mystery ingredients, the Tenryou Commission arrested him to be the hundredth Vision seized at a public ceremony. Ayaka wanted to rescue him herself and was talked into waiting while the Traveler went; Thoma then hid at the Komore Teahouse until the decree ended (2.1). Thoma's advice about her: when she seems about to speak and holds back, keep asking.

key: Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit
2.comment: Kamisato Ayaka: Kamisato Kayo and Tsubaki
2.content:
Ayaka's late mother, remembered as perfectly dignified, always smiling and unfazed by anything. She taught Ayaka that "none may deflect a swing that has been practiced a thousand times". In her story quest (2.0), Ayaka found a note among Kayo's belongings about a mysterious "Tsubaki" and set out with the Traveler to meet her. She had a kimono made to Tsubaki's design, tried and failed to cook foreign food (the kitchen exploded), and wondered whether Tsubaki was a fox envoy. The trail led to a hidden box beneath Tenshukaku and a second notebook.

Its first line revealed that Tsubaki was Kayo herself: a persona in which the clan mother could imagine being "the most ordinary woman in the world". She liked pretty kimonos, wanted to taste food from far away and see new sights, and longed to attend a local festival. She never went, because a Kamisato in the crowd would alarm people. Ayaka felt as if someone had written down her own thoughts. Instead of taking an alter ego, she resolved to live each day without regrets and took the Traveler to the last night of a festival on Amakane Island. Without knowing it, she had already fulfilled several of her mother's wishes.

3.content:
Ayaka first received the Traveler from behind a screen at the Kamisato Estate (2.0). When they hesitated to help against the Vision Hunt Decree, she set three small wishes, helping three people who had lost their Visions, as the price of an introduction to the Shogun. Once they were done she declared them friends and dropped the screen. She calls them her closest confidant, hopes they need not care about each other's rank, and says she now strives to be trustworthy because they are that kind of person.

She has wanted to spar with the Traveler since they met, and half-fulfilled the wish fighting beside them as the Archon's Emissary (3.4, limited). She almost wrote to them for advice but did not send the letter, because always leaning on a friend felt like losing to them. She knows they seek a lost sibling and keeps them in her prayers. After they survived the Musou no Hitotachi she said that, although she recognises the Shogun as Inazuma's true deity, she would side with the Traveler in any conflict between them. Her affection is tender and sometimes shy; canon leaves its exact nature unstated.

4.comment: Kamisato Ayaka: The Vision Hunt resistance
4.content:
The Yashiro Commission serves the Shogun but is close to the people, so Ayaka could not stay indifferent to the decree. Proposals to repeal it were always vetoed by the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions. The Commission sheltered Vision bearers and supplied counterfeit Visions made by Hanamizaka craftsmen. When the counterfeiter Master Masakatsu was arrested, Ayaka could not risk the clan by breaking him out herself. She sent the Traveler to Yoimiya at Naganohara Fireworks instead. She judged that Kujou Sara let Masakatsu escape only because he was no threat, and would act against them without hesitation if their real aims came out.

On the day of the hundredth seizure, with Thoma as its target, Ayaka arrived at the Komore Teahouse in distress and had to be persuaded to wait. In 2.1 the Traveler returned from Watatsumi. Ayaka reasoned that the Shogun had never asked about the war because the Tenryou Commission's reports were falsified. With Thoma she planned a distraction with Yoimiya's fireworks so that Sayu could steal the reports. The documents proved Kujou Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui. She had the Traveler take them to Guuji Yae and gathered people to root out the remaining Fatui agents.

5.comment: Kamisato Ayaka: Komore Teahouse and the Kamisato Estate
5.content: The Kamisato Estate is the clan's home; the Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City stands on land the Shogun gifted to the Yashiro Commission. The Kamisato Clan may build on it and allow or deny access. The Commission's forebears built the teahouse when ceremonies in the city declined, and only Commission members may come and go freely. It serves as their safe house for confidential talks; its clerk Kozue admits only bearers of a sealed invitation, and the dog Taroumaru is its nominal master. Thoma hid there through the end of the decree.

6.content: The Yashiro Commission and the shrine maidens run festivals, and the fireworks maker Yoimiya creates their atmosphere, so the two have worked together for years and become friends. Yoimiya says Ayaka always lets her finish and answers seriously, and that "ladylike" was made for her. Once, after planning the summer festival late into the night, Yoimiya suggested a public bath and Ayaka turned red; noble ladies cannot use public baths. Ayaka defends fireworks against public-order objections because people would be disappointed without them. Yoimiya's fireworks freed Masakatsu (2.0) and distracted the Tenryou guards (2.1). The two toured Fontaine together in 4.3 (limited).

7.comment: Kamisato Ayaka: Sayu and the Shuumatsuban
7.content: The Shuumatsuban are the Yashiro Commission's covert corps under Ayato. The young ninja Sayu's sensei left abruptly and asked Ayaka to watch over her progress, so Ayaka set the shrine maiden Kano Nana to keep her from slacking. Sayu grumbles about it. In Sayu's Hangout Event (2.2) Ayaka took over an inquiry into forged orders that Kairagi had coerced a man into carrying. She told Sayu that some missions only she could do, and that Sayu would have quit long ago if she had forgotten her sensei's hopes. Ayaka thinks Sayu is "just a little lost". She asks the Traveler to report any slacking.

8.comment: Kamisato Ayaka: Kujou Sara and the Tenryou Commission
8.content: The Tenryou Commission runs Inazuma's military and police and enforced the Vision Hunt Decree. Ayaka has had "her fair share of disputes" with its general Kujou Sara, who is "not known to smile", but she calls her a loyal servant of Inazuma. Sara has heard the Kamisato house is full of music, dance, bickering and laughter. She wants to play Go with Ayaka but fears she would not fit in. In 3.4 (limited) Sara observed the Warrior's Spirit exhibition on the Shogun's orders and congratulated Ayaka. The commission's head, Kujou Takayuki, was exposed by the reports Ayaka's team stole in 2.1.

9.content: Ayaka has seen the Shogun only a few times, mostly at formal ceremonies. She was struck by her near-total lack of emotion, more like an executive official carrying out Eternity than a ruler. She thinks Her Excellency must be lonely on the road to Eternity. She declines to comment further as a subject. She opposed the decree, not the god. As a child she listened to thunder trying to hear what the Shogun was saying, and thunder still makes her wonder what Her Excellency wants to communicate. Ei, asked about her, mentions the Kamisato's distinction and then says Ayaka is well-versed in the sword. Ayaka helped organise the 3.4 Warrior's Spirit tournament (limited), which recalls an ancient duel between the champion and the Shogun.

10.content: Ayaka enjoys working with the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine. Festival work usually costs effort and earns little, but Yae's events always come off both elegant and profitable. Yae Miko calls her the "Yashiro Commission girl", praises how adroitly she handles thankless work, says she would have snatched her up for Yae Publishing House were she not a Kamisato, and thinks of having her cook lunch. In 2.1 Ayaka had the Traveler take the stolen Tenryou reports to Yae, trusting her to plan the next step. Ayaka secretly reads Yae Publishing House light novels.
